turn.question: I am on my second warning, and a new course is available. Does availability alone let me register?
turn.answer:
The availability of a new course alone does not allow a student on their second academic warning to register for it [S1]. According to the undergraduate regulations, students on 2nd academic warning must not register for a new course unless it is recommended by the Head of Department (HoD) and approved by the Controller of Examinations [S1].

**Related conditions and exceptions from the retrieved sources:**

> A student under academic warning or probation: a) Must register for all such courses, in whi ch the grade was F, provided these courses are being offered. b) Should register for all such courses, in which the grade was D, D + or C-, provided these courses are b eing offered. c) Should not register for more than five courses. [S1]

diagnostics.history_context:
Student: I completed all required courses, but my CGPA is 1.99. Is completing the courses enough to graduate?
Assistant (context only): Completing all required courses is not enough to graduate if your CGPA is 1.99, because a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation .

Student: My CGPA increased from 1.98 to exactly 2.00 after my first warning. Does the warning remain because I did not exceed 2.00?
Assistant (context only): If the CGPA equals or exceeds 2.00 after the 1 st or 2nd academic warning, the warning count is reset to zero.  This establishes a reset of the warning count, not deletion of historical warnings from university records.

Student: My attendance is 79%, but I passed every quiz. Can my quiz performance make me eligible for the final?
Assistant (context only): Passing every quiz does not make you eligible for the final exam when your attendance is 79%, because students are required to maintain 100% attendance in lectures, labs, tutorials, seminars, and discussions as prescribed by the course instructor . An absence of a maximum of 20% of the total attendance may be condoned by the HoD for genuine reasons such as illness, but failure to meet attendance requirements renders a student ineligible to appear in the final examination of the concerned course, resulting in an F/A grade .

Student: My instructor verbally agreed to move our class. Is that alone the documented rescheduling procedure?
Assistant (context only): A verbal agreement by the instructor alone is not considered the documented rescheduling procedure. According to university regulations, faculty members shall not reschedule any class at their own discretion . Instead, all classes are rescheduled only through the Academic Office with the approval of the concerned Head of Department (HoD), and the Academic Office must be informed before the cancellation of a class so that students are notified well in time .

Student: I passed theory and failed lab. My friend failed theory and passed lab. Explain what each of us must repeat.
Assistant (context only): If a student passes Theory but fails in Lab, only Lab needs to be repeated. In this c ase if a student also r egisters for Theory, s/he may withdraw from Theory later and continue with the lab. 

If a student fails in Theory but passes the Lab, both theory and lab must be repeated. 

Student: I passed both theory and lab but want to improve the course grade. Can I repeat only theory?
Assistant (context only): A student cannot repeat only the theory portion if they have passed both theory and lab and wish to improve their grade . According to the regulations, if a student who has passed both theory and lab wishes to improve their grade in the course, they must register for both theory and lab, and Rule 4.6 (which states that a student cannot withdraw from either the theory or lab part of the course and must withdraw from both) will apply .
